visual.general_description: Grayscale frontal infant chest radiograph with looped tubing, an L marker and a small symbol at the lower right.
visual.detailed_description: Large grayscale frontal chest radiograph of an infant including shoulders and upper arms. A white letter L is printed in the upper right and a small double-headed arrow symbol in the lower right corner. Two corrugated tubes descend from the top of the image on the left of the spine, one ending in a bright tip with several small prongs; a round coil of thin tubing lies at the upper left chest and a long thin tube curves in a wide loop around the lower left of the image. Both lung fields are gray with darker air-filled bands between ribs and patchy hazy regions, and the heart shadow lies near the middle. No arrow overlay, names or dates are printed. The arrangement of tubes, ribs and markers looks the same as the radiograph in Figure 5 of the article, which carries an overlay arrow; no text states they are the same image.
